tm_s01.title: Unauthenticated access to an exposed component
tm_s01.why: It receives traffic from the internet and isn't marked as authenticated: anyone can call it.
tm_s01.mitigation_1: Require authentication on every non-public route
tm_s01.mitigation_2: Keep an explicit inventory of public routes

tm_s02.title: Tokens or sessions accepted without proper validation
tm_s02.why: The system trusts the identity this provider issues: always check the signature, issuer, audience and expiry.
tm_s02.mitigation_1: Validate signature, iss, aud and exp; reject alg=none
tm_s02.mitigation_2: Rotate keys and revoke sessions on sign-out

tm_s03.title: Spoofable webhooks or third-party calls
tm_s03.why: A third-party service sends data to this component: without verifying the signature, anyone can pretend to be it.
tm_s03.mitigation_1: Verify the webhook's HMAC signature and timestamp
tm_s03.mitigation_2: Make processing idempotent by event ID

tm_s04.title: Requests made on the user's behalf (CSRF)
tm_s04.why: A web app with a browser session can receive requests forged from another origin.
tm_s04.mitigation_1: SameSite=Strict/Lax cookies plus an anti-CSRF token or header

tm_t01.title: Injection through the component's input
tm_t01.why: It processes input it doesn't control: queries, commands, templates or HTML built from it can be altered.
tm_t01.mitigation_1: Parameterized queries and APIs that don't go through a shell
tm_t01.mitigation_2: Allow-list validation and context-aware output encoding

tm_t02.title: Vulnerable or compromised dependencies
tm_t02.why: The component is built from third-party code: a vulnerable version or a malicious package changes how it behaves.
tm_t02.mitigation_1: Upgrade to fixed versions and pin them with a lockfile
tm_t02.mitigation_2: Check KEV/EPSS and monitor the supply chain

tm_t03.title: Unauthenticated writes to the data store
tm_t03.why: Some flow writes to this store without authentication: anyone with network access can alter the data.
tm_t03.mitigation_2: Isolate the store on a private network

tm_t04.title: Data tampering in transit
tm_t04.why: The flow crosses a trust boundary unencrypted: an attacker in the middle can modify it.
tm_t04.mitigation_1: TLS on every flow that crosses a boundary
tm_t04.mitigation_2: Validate certificates; HSTS on anything exposed

tm_r01.title: Sensitive actions without a verifiable trail
tm_r01.why: It handles sensitive data: without a record of who did what, abuse can't be investigated or attributed.
tm_r01.mitigation_1: Audit log of access and changes (who, what, when)
tm_r01.mitigation_2: Logs out of reach of whoever operates the app

tm_i01.title: Secrets or sensitive data exposed by the component
tm_i01.why: A component can leak information through errors, overly broad responses or secrets in the code.
tm_i01.mitigation_1: Generic errors to the outside, details only in logs
tm_i01.mitigation_2: Secrets in a secrets manager, never in the repository
tm_i01.mitigation_3: Responses with only the fields needed

tm_i02.title: Sensitive data unencrypted at rest
tm_i02.why: It stores sensitive data and isn't marked as encrypted at rest: a copy of the disk or a backup exposes it.
tm_i02.mitigation_1: Encryption at rest with managed keys (KMS)
tm_i02.mitigation_2: Minimize and pseudonymize what you store

tm_i03.title: Credentials stored in recoverable form
tm_i03.why: It stores credentials: with weak or reversible hashes, a database leak becomes a password leak.
tm_i03.mitigation_1: Hash passwords with scrypt, Argon2id or bcrypt

tm_i04.title: Data readable in transit
tm_i04.why: The flow crosses a trust boundary unencrypted and carries non-public data.
tm_i04.mitigation_2: Never send credentials or personal data over cleartext channels

tm_i05.title: Sensitive data sent to a third party
tm_i05.why: The flow carries personal data, payment data or credentials to an external service: they leave your control.
tm_i05.mitigation_1: Send only what's essential and pseudonymize it
tm_i05.mitigation_2: Data processing agreement and vendor review

tm_i06.title: Objects accessible without permission
tm_i06.why: A misconfigured file store serves objects to anyone who has the link.
tm_i06.mitigation_1: Private buckets and short-lived signed URLs
tm_i06.mitigation_2: Block public access at the account level

tm_d01.title: Resource exhaustion from request volume
tm_d01.why: It's exposed to the internet: without limits, a few expensive requests are enough to take it down.

tm_d02.title: Third-party dependency without a failure plan
tm_d02.why: If the external service goes down or slows down, the component that calls it can hang along with it.
tm_d02.mitigation_1: Timeouts, retries with backoff and a circuit breaker

tm_e01.title: Access to other users' objects or functions
tm_e01.why: It tells users apart: without checking object ownership and role on every request, one user reaches another's data (BOLA/BFLA).
tm_e01.mitigation_1: Server-side, per-object authorization on every request
tm_e01.mitigation_2: Deny by default and test with two users

tm_e02.title: The server sends requests wherever the attacker chooses (SSRF)
tm_e02.why: This component calls other services: if part of the destination comes from input, it can reach the internal network or cloud metadata.
tm_e02.mitigation_1: Allow-list destinations and pin DNS resolution

pv_l01.title: One person's records can be linked
pv_l01.why: This store keeps personal data with stable identifiers: records about the same person can be joined across tables, services or exports to rebuild their profile.
pv_l01.mitigation_1: Context-specific identifiers (pseudonyms) instead of a single global one
pv_l01.mitigation_2: Minimize persistent identifiers and keep datasets separate

pv_i01.title: Re-identification of "anonymized" data
pv_i01.why: Exported or aggregated personal data can identify someone again when combined with other sources.
pv_i01.mitigation_2: Don't share raw data for analytics or testing

pv_nr01.title: More is kept than needed about what each person does
pv_nr01.why: A process that handles personal data can log actions in so much detail that users can no longer deny or conceal what they did, even when they should be able to.
pv_nr01.mitigation_1: Log only what's needed to operate and audit
pv_nr01.mitigation_2: Set log retention periods and pseudonymize users in logs

pv_d01.title: Others can tell whether someone uses the service
pv_d01.why: Different responses (e.g. "that email is already registered"), timing or metadata reveal to a third party whether a person has an account or what they do.
pv_d01.mitigation_1: Uniform messages and response times for sign-up, sign-in and account recovery

pv_dd01.title: Personal data sent to a third party
pv_dd01.why: This flow carries personal data to a third-party service: you lose control over how it's used, how long it's kept and which country it ends up in.
pv_dd01.mitigation_1: Send only the fields that are essential
pv_dd01.mitigation_2: Data processing agreement and review of international transfers

pv_dd02.title: Personal data readable if the store leaks
pv_dd02.why: It stores personal data without encryption at rest: a backup or improper access exposes it as is.
pv_dd02.mitigation_2: Field-level encryption for the most sensitive data

pv_u01.title: People don't know what's done with their data and can't decide
pv_u01.why: A component collects personal data directly from users: without clear notice, consent where it applies and a way to view, correct or delete their data, they can't exercise control.
pv_u01.mitigation_1: Privacy notice at the point of collection
pv_u01.mitigation_2: Self-service to access, export and delete their own data

pv_nc01.title: Processing without a legal basis, retention period or record
pv_nc01.why: A store of personal data needs a documented purpose, legal basis and retention period; without them you're out of compliance (GDPR, local laws).
pv_nc01.mitigation_1: Record of processing activities and a retention policy with automatic deletion
pv_nc01.mitigation_2: Data protection impact assessment (DPIA) if the processing is high risk
